facts.topic: Alpine Holy Saturday Easter fires on mountain heights

fact.en: In some Alpine regions, Easter fires were lit high on the mountains around Holy Saturday.
fact.fr: Dans certaines régions alpines, on allumait des feux de Pâques sur les hauteurs vers le Samedi saint.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Polish joyful Alleluia Easter greeting

fact.en: Polish Easter greetings once included the joyful formula Wesołego Alleluja.
fact.fr: Les salutations polonaises de Pâques comprenaient la formule joyeuse Wesołego Alleluja.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Easter walking pilgrimage with Cross and prayer

fact.en: Older Easter walks through the fields could include carrying a crucifix and praying together.
fact.fr: D'anciennes promenades pascales dans les champs pouvaient comporter le port d'un crucifix et des prières communes.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Easter open house and family visits

fact.en: Some families marked Easter with an open house, welcoming relatives and neighbors to festive meals.
fact.fr: Certaines familles fêtaient Pâques en ouvrant leur maison aux parents et voisins pour des repas de fête.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

region: European Catholic and wider Christian homes

facts.topic: Easter Monday visits to grandparents

fact.en: In parts of French Canada, Easter Monday visits to grandparents were connected with the journey to Emmaus.
fact.fr: Dans certaines régions du Canada français, les visites aux grands-parents le lundi de Pâques étaient rapprochées du chemin d'Emmaüs.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Easter Friday pilgrimage to local shrine

fact.en: On the Friday after Easter, regional pilgrimages sometimes went to a nearby shrine on foot or horseback.
fact.fr: Le vendredi après Pâques, des pèlerinages régionaux se rendaient parfois à un sanctuaire voisin à pied ou à cheval.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Low Sunday First Communion candle procession

fact.en: Some historical Low Sunday First Communions used white garments and processions with lighted candles.
fact.fr: Certaines premières communions du dimanche in albis comportaient autrefois vêtements blancs et processions avec des cierges allumés.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Easter lamb-shaped pastries and table figures

fact.en: Easter lambs were fashioned not only from pastry but sometimes from butter or sugar for the family table.
fact.fr: On façonnait des agneaux de Pâques non seulement en pâtisserie, mais aussi parfois en beurre ou en sucre pour la table familiale.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Giving decorated Easter eggs to children and household staff

fact.en: Decorated Easter eggs were historically presented to children and household workers as gifts.
fact.fr: Les œufs de Pâques décorés étaient autrefois offerts aux enfants et aux employés de maison.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Red or coloured Easter eggs in regional celebrations

fact.en: Red and green Easter eggs coexisted with regional Christian symbolism and separate folk beliefs.
fact.fr: Les œufs de Pâques rouges et verts associaient selon les régions symbolisme chrétien et croyances populaires distinctes.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Easter egg hunt traditions

fact.en: Easter egg hunts and games belonged to family tradition rather than to the Church's official rites.
fact.fr: La chasse aux œufs et les jeux de Pâques relevaient des traditions familiales, non des rites officiels de l'Église.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Shared blessed Easter egg at family breakfast

fact.en: Some Slavic families divided a single blessed Easter egg among everyone at breakfast.
fact.fr: Dans certaines familles slaves, on partageait un seul œuf pascal béni entre tous les convives au petit déjeuner.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Easter paska bread decorated with crosses

fact.en: Some traditional paska Easter loaves carried a cross on their crust.
fact.fr: Certains pains traditionnels de Pâques appelés paska portaient une croix sur leur croûte.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Osterstollen and Austrian Easter cross loaves

fact.en: Austrian Easter loaves and Osterstollen formed distinct regional types of festive bread.
fact.fr: Les pains de Pâques autrichiens et l'Osterstollen représentaient des variantes régionales de pains de fête.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Polish mazurki and South German Easter cakes

fact.en: Polish mazurki were among the regional cakes served at Easter.
fact.fr: Les mazurki polonais figuraient parmi les gâteaux régionaux servis à Pâques.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Historical Ascension walking procession recalling Bethany

fact.en: Some historical Ascension processions evoked the journey from Bethany toward the Mount of Olives.
fact.fr: Certaines anciennes processions de l'Ascension évoquaient le trajet depuis Béthanie vers le mont des Oliviers.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Field and pasture blessing on Ascension

fact.en: Ascension processions in some communities included prayers for fields and pastureland.
fact.fr: Dans certaines communautés, les processions de l'Ascension comportaient des prières pour les champs et les pâturages.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

region: Some German and central European communities

facts.topic: Ascension games and races

fact.en: Historical Ascension festivities could include outdoor races and games as well as religious observance.
fact.fr: Les fêtes anciennes de l'Ascension pouvaient mêler courses et jeux de plein air aux pratiques religieuses.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Historical Pentecost trumpet blasts during the sequence

fact.en: In medieval Pentecost celebrations, trumpet blasts could accompany the sequence as dramatic symbolism.
fact.fr: Dans certaines célébrations médiévales de la Pentecôte, des sonneries de trompettes accompagnaient la séquence à titre de symbole dramatique.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Releasing doves during Pentecost church observances

fact.en: Certain medieval churches released living doves during Pentecost ceremonies to evoke the Holy Spirit.
fact.fr: Certaines églises médiévales libéraient de vraies colombes pendant les cérémonies de Pentecôte pour évoquer le Saint-Esprit.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Wooden Holy Ghost dove over family dining table

fact.en: A wooden dove symbolizing the Holy Spirit could once hang over a family's Pentecost dining table.
fact.fr: Une colombe de bois symbolisant le Saint-Esprit pouvait autrefois être suspendue au-dessus de la table familiale à la Pentecôte.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Whitsun cracking whips and firing salutes

fact.en: Some older Pentecost village celebrations featured whip-cracking or noisy salutes.
fact.fr: Certaines anciennes fêtes villageoises de la Pentecôte comportaient des claquements de fouets ou des salves bruyantes.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: May Queen and Pentecost Bride spring pageants

fact.en: Pentecost celebrations in parts of Europe included a spring pageant with a Pentecost Bride.
fact.fr: Dans certaines régions d'Europe, les fêtes de Pentecôte comprenaient un cortège printanier avec une « fiancée de Pentecôte ».

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

region: European spring folk culture, mixed religious origin

facts.topic: Pentecost Vigil blessing flowers, fields and fruit trees

fact.en: Historical Pentecost Vigil practices sometimes included blessing flowers, fields or fruit trees.
fact.fr: D'anciennes pratiques de la vigile de Pentecôte comprenaient parfois la bénédiction de fleurs, champs ou arbres fruitiers.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

region: Reported Christian rural Central European practice

facts.topic: Sign of the Cross during ordinary household work on Trinity Sunday

fact.en: Some households made the Sign of the Cross over everyday work on Trinity Sunday as a voluntary devotion.
fact.fr: Certains foyers traçaient le signe de croix sur les travaux ordinaires le dimanche de la Trinité, par dévotion volontaire.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Holy Trinity public plague columns

fact.en: Public Holy Trinity columns in Central Europe could commemorate deliverance from plague.
fact.fr: Des colonnes publiques de la Sainte Trinité en Europe centrale pouvaient commémorer une délivrance de la peste.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Adoration as Corpus Christi procession passes a home

fact.en: Families along a Corpus Christi procession route could adore the Blessed Sacrament from their doorways.
fact.fr: Des familles bordant une procession de la Fête-Dieu pouvaient adorer le Saint-Sacrement depuis leur porte.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Corpus Christi windows adorned with candles and sacred images

fact.en: Windows along Corpus Christi procession routes were sometimes adorned with candles and sacred images.
fact.fr: Les fenêtres longeant les processions de la Fête-Dieu étaient parfois ornées de cierges et d'images saintes.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

region: France Spain Portugal Belgium Italy and elsewhere

facts.topic: Birch greenery decorating Corpus Christi homes and routes

fact.en: Birch branches once decorated houses and streets along Corpus Christi processions in some regions.
fact.fr: Des branches de bouleau décoraient autrefois les maisons et rues sur le parcours de processions de la Fête-Dieu.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Gigantes y Cabezudos in Corpus Christi festivities

fact.en: Spanish Corpus Christi festivities could include giant costumed figures called Gigantes y Cabezudos.
fact.fr: Les fêtes espagnoles de la Fête-Dieu pouvaient comprendre de grands personnages costumés appelés Gigantes y Cabezudos.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Seville boys' Corpus Christi dance

fact.en: In Seville, a dance by cathedral choirboys formed a distinctive local Corpus Christi custom.
fact.fr: À Séville, une danse des enfants de chœur de la cathédrale constituait une coutume locale particulière de la Fête-Dieu.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Flower wreaths for Corpus Christi homes, flags and banners

fact.en: Flower wreaths could decorate Corpus Christi banners, houses and poles, apart from the Eucharistic rite itself.
fact.fr: Des couronnes de fleurs pouvaient orner bannières, maisons et perches pour la Fête-Dieu, indépendamment du rite eucharistique.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Hanging blessed Corpus Christi wreaths at home or by fields

fact.en: In some Polish places, blessed Corpus Christi wreaths were later hung in houses or near fields.
fact.fr: En certains lieux de Pologne, les couronnes bénies à la Fête-Dieu étaient ensuite suspendues dans les maisons ou près des champs.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Kyrie-o-ole sung as the last harvest wagon comes home

fact.en: A historical harvest song called Kyrie-o-le was sung as the last wagon returned from the fields.
fact.fr: Un ancien chant de moisson appelé Kyrie-o-le était entonné au retour du dernier chariot des champs.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Decorating a cross-shaped last sheaf of grain

fact.en: In southern France, the last sheaf of grain was sometimes tied into a cross and decorated.
fact.fr: Dans le sud de la France, la dernière gerbe de céréales était parfois nouée en croix et décorée.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Polish harvest wreaths presented for blessing

fact.en: Some Polish rural communities brought decorated harvest wreaths in procession for a priest's blessing.
fact.fr: Certaines communautés rurales polonaises apportaient des couronnes de moisson en procession pour les faire bénir par un prêtre.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Saint Martin goose at the family table

fact.en: A goose dinner became a historical food tradition associated with Saint Martin's Day.
fact.fr: Le repas d'oie est devenu une ancienne tradition culinaire liée à la Saint-Martin.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Tasting new harvest wine at Martinmas

fact.en: In some places, the first wine of the new harvest was tasted at Saint Martin's feast.
fact.fr: En certains lieux, on goûtait le vin nouveau à la fête de saint Martin.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Kirchweih/Kirmes church patron or dedication festivities

fact.en: German Kirchweih or Kirmes festivities historically combined a church's dedication or patronal feast with local celebrations.
fact.fr: Les Kirchweih ou Kirmes allemandes associaient autrefois la dédicace ou la fête patronale d'une église à des réjouissances locales.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Household name-day exemption from chores

fact.en: On some Catholic name days, the person being celebrated was excused from household chores.
fact.fr: Lors de certaines fêtes du prénom, la personne célébrée était dispensée des tâches domestiques.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Anniversary pilgrimage to a martyr's tomb

fact.en: Early Christians commemorated martyrs by visiting their tombs, especially on their death anniversaries.
fact.fr: Les premiers chrétiens commémoraient les martyrs en visitant leurs tombeaux, notamment au jour anniversaire de leur mort.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Public ceremonial translation of saints' relics

fact.en: The solemn arrival of a saint's relics could once be accompanied by both church and civic processions.
fact.fr: L'arrivée solennelle des reliques d'un saint pouvait autrefois s'accompagner de processions religieuses et civiles.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Assumption field procession with priest

fact.en: Historical Assumption observances in Austria sometimes included priest-led processions to pray for the harvest.
fact.fr: En Autriche, certaines anciennes célébrations de l'Assomption comprenaient des processions conduites par un prêtre pour prier pour les récoltes.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Sicilian two-week fruit abstinence and Assumption fruit blessing

fact.en: In one older Sicilian Assumption practice, abstaining from fruit beforehand made a later fruit blessing especially meaningful.
fact.fr: Dans une ancienne pratique sicilienne de l'Assomption, l'abstinence de fruits avant la fête donnait une portée particulière à leur bénédiction.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Blessing countryside and fields on Assumption

fact.en: Some local Assumption celebrations included blessings of fields and countryside.
fact.fr: Certaines célébrations locales de l'Assomption comportaient des bénédictions des champs et de la campagne.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Alpine Assumption pasture and livestock blessing

fact.en: In Alpine areas, blessings of mountain livestock could be associated with Assumption celebrations.
fact.fr: Dans les régions alpines, des bénédictions du bétail de montagne pouvaient accompagner les fêtes de l'Assomption.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Blessing fishing vessels and sea at Assumption

fact.en: Some Portuguese coastal communities included boats or the sea in local Assumption blessings.
fact.fr: Certaines communautés côtières portugaises associaient barques ou mer aux bénédictions locales de l'Assomption.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

region: Portugal and some North American coastal towns

facts.topic: Immaculate Conception novenas and processions

fact.en: Spanish Immaculate Conception feasts historically included regional novenas, vigils and processions.
fact.fr: Les fêtes espagnoles de l'Immaculée Conception comprenaient autrefois des neuvaines, veillées et processions régionales.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Taking down Christmas crib on Candlemas

fact.en: Some families kept the Christmas crib until Candlemas, although that did not change the official liturgical season.
fact.fr: Certaines familles gardaient la crèche jusqu'à la Chandeleur sans que cela modifie le temps liturgique officiel.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Historical Annunciation Golden Mass pageant

fact.en: Older Annunciation celebrations could stage a dramatic Golden Mass depicting the Angel Gabriel.
fact.fr: D'anciennes fêtes de l'Annonciation pouvaient mettre en scène une « messe d'or » dramatique figurant l'ange Gabriel.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Suspended Gabriel figure or child in Annunciation pageant

fact.en: In some medieval Annunciation pageants, an image representing Gabriel was suspended above the congregation.
fact.fr: Dans certaines représentations médiévales de l'Annonciation, une image de Gabriel était suspendue au-dessus des fidèles.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Priest-blessed Annunciation wheat wafer shared at home

fact.en: A regional Annunciation custom shared a priest-blessed wheat wafer at home.
fact.fr: Une coutume régionale de l'Annonciation consistait à partager à la maison une galette de blé bénie par un prêtre.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Annunciation image placed among seed grain with prayer

fact.en: Some Central European farmers placed an Annunciation image among seed grain while praying to Our Lady.
fact.fr: Certains agriculteurs d'Europe centrale plaçaient une image de l'Annonciation parmi les semences en priant la Vierge.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Our Lady of Grape Harvest household feast

fact.en: A French grape-harvest devotion on 8 September included blessing and eating the first grapes.
fact.fr: Une dévotion française liée aux vendanges, le 8 septembre, comprenait la bénédiction et la dégustation des premiers raisins.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Seventh- and thirtieth-day prayers for deceased

fact.en: Masses for the dead have historically been offered on the seventh and thirtieth days after death in some traditions.
fact.fr: Dans certaines traditions, des messes pour les défunts étaient célébrées les septième et trentième jours après le décès.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Cleaning and decorating graves before All Souls

fact.en: Before All Souls, families in some places cleaned and decorated their relatives' graves.
fact.fr: Avant la Commémoration des fidèles défunts, des familles nettoyaient et ornaient en certains lieux les tombes de leurs proches.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: All Souls graveside lanterns and votive candles

fact.en: Lanterns and protected candles were placed at graves around All Saints and All Souls in some countries.
fact.fr: Dans certains pays, on déposait des lanternes et des cierges protégés sur les tombes à la Toussaint et au jour des Défunts.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Bell tolling at All Saints dusk to summon prayer

fact.en: Church bells at dusk on All Saints once summoned some Central European communities to pray for the dead.
fact.fr: En Europe centrale, des cloches sonnaient autrefois au crépuscule de la Toussaint pour inviter à prier pour les défunts.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: All Souls family prayer by a retained Candlemas candle

fact.en: Some families preserved a blessed Candlemas candle and lit it when praying for the dead at All Souls.
fact.fr: Certaines familles conservaient un cierge béni à la Chandeleur et l'allumaient pour prier pour les défunts.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Breton overnight prayer bells and farmhouse visits

fact.en: In parts of Brittany, nighttime bell-ringers visited farmhouses to call for prayers for the dead.
fact.fr: Dans certaines régions de Bretagne, des sonneurs parcouraient les fermes la nuit pour inviter à prier pour les morts.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Brazilian All Souls cemetery visit and candles

fact.en: Brazilian All Souls observances historically included cemetery visits, prayers and candles.
fact.fr: Au Brésil, les anciennes pratiques du jour des Défunts comprenaient visites au cimetière, prières et cierges.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Philippine grave repair preceding All Souls novena

fact.en: In the Philippines, families repaired graves in preparation for an All Souls novena.
fact.fr: Aux Philippines, des familles entretenaient les tombes en vue d'une neuvaine pour les défunts.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Philippine door-to-door souls' carolling for sweets

fact.en: Philippine All Souls observances also included door-to-door songs for small treats in some localities.
fact.fr: Dans certaines localités philippines, le souvenir des défunts s'accompagnait aussi de chants de porte en porte pour recevoir des friandises.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: All Souls soul bread given to poor and children

fact.en: For All Souls, some communities gave special soul breads to children or people in need.
fact.fr: Pour le jour des Défunts, certaines communautés distribuaient des pains particuliers aux enfants ou aux personnes dans le besoin.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

region: France Belgium Central Europe and elsewhere

facts.topic: Inviting Hungarian orphans to All Souls family meals

fact.en: In some Hungarian households, orphaned children were invited to meals around All Souls.
fact.fr: Dans certains foyers hongrois, des enfants orphelins étaient invités aux repas de la période des Défunts.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Saint Blaise blessed bread sticks / pan bendito

fact.en: Saint Blaise's day had regional blessed-bread customs distinct from the official throat blessing.
fact.fr: La Saint-Blaise connaissait des coutumes régionales de pain béni distinctes de la bénédiction officielle des gorges.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Croagh Patrick and Lough Derg penitential pilgrimages

fact.en: Irish penitential pilgrimage traditions include Croagh Patrick and Lough Derg, with different local observances.
fact.fr: Les traditions irlandaises de pèlerinage pénitentiel comprennent Croagh Patrick et Lough Derg, aux pratiques locales différentes.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Wearing green and shamrock for Saint Patrick

fact.en: Wearing a shamrock for Saint Patrick's Day is historical Irish custom; its precise catechetical origin remains legendary.
fact.fr: Porter du trèfle à la Saint-Patrick est une coutume irlandaise ancienne, dont l'origine catéchétique précise reste légendaire.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Saint Patrick's Breastplate prayer observance

fact.en: Saint Patrick's Breastplate, or Lorica, became a devotional prayer despite uncertainty over its historical authorship.
fact.fr: La cuirasse de saint Patrick, ou Lorica, est devenue une prière de dévotion malgré l'incertitude sur son auteur historique.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Saint Joseph fritelli and festival breads

fact.en: Saint Joseph's Day food traditions sometimes paired small festival breads with charity for the poor.
fact.fr: Certaines traditions culinaires de la Saint-Joseph associaient de petits pains de fête à la charité envers les pauvres.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Fisherfolk Saint Anthony mast shrine

fact.en: Some Basque sailors historically kept a small shrine to Saint Anthony on a ship's mast.
fact.fr: Certains marins basques installaient autrefois un petit sanctuaire dédié à saint Antoine sur le mât de leur bateau.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Tuesday Saint Anthony novena

fact.en: Tuesday devotions and continuing novenas to Saint Anthony appear in historical Catholic practice.
fact.fr: Des dévotions du mardi et des neuvaines permanentes à saint Antoine sont attestées dans l'histoire catholique.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Lisbon Saint Anthony day household shrines

fact.en: Lisbon households once decorated Saint Anthony images and small shrines for his June feast.
fact.fr: Des foyers de Lisbonne décoraient autrefois images et petits autels de saint Antoine pour sa fête de juin.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Breton fishermen's Saint John fires and crew prayers

fact.en: Breton fishermen's Saint John's Eve festivities could include fires on boat masts, prayer and singing.
fact.fr: En Bretagne, les fêtes des pêcheurs à la veille de la Saint-Jean pouvaient réunir feux sur les mâts, prières et chants.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Blessing Peter and Paul feast grain

fact.en: Historical Saint Peter and Paul's Day gatherings in some places included blessing grain from the harvest.
fact.fr: Dans certains lieux, les anciennes fêtes de saint Pierre et saint Paul comprenaient la bénédiction de céréales récoltées.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Hanging blessed straw crowns above the dining table

fact.en: Straw crowns blessed around Saint Peter and Paul's feast were sometimes hung above the dining table.
fact.fr: Des couronnes de paille bénies autour de la fête de saint Pierre et saint Paul étaient parfois suspendues au-dessus de la table.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Saint Christopher mural above doors or at church walls

fact.en: Large Saint Christopher images were historically painted over doorways or on exterior church walls.
fact.fr: De grandes images de saint Christophe étaient autrefois peintes au-dessus des portes ou sur les murs extérieurs des églises.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Carrying a blessed Saint Christopher medal when travelling

fact.en: Travelers sometimes carried blessed Saint Christopher medals separately from any blessing of vehicles.
fact.fr: Des voyageurs portaient parfois des médailles bénies de saint Christophe, distinctement de toute bénédiction du véhicule.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Saint Anne de Beaupré pilgrimage in Québec

fact.en: Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupré in Québec became a historic pilgrimage destination for devotion to Saint Anne.
fact.fr: Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupré, au Québec, devint un lieu de pèlerinage historique dédié à sainte Anne.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

facts.topic: Saint Lucy white-robed bride and candle wreath breakfast

fact.en: A Scandinavian Saint Lucy household custom involved a white-robed girl wearing a candle wreath and serving breakfast.
fact.fr: Une coutume scandinave de la Sainte-Lucie mettait en scène une jeune fille vêtue de blanc, portant une couronne de bougies et servant le petit déjeuner.

source.book: Francis X. Weiser, Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)
